newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier, may turn lower later.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier, may turn lower later.

text.p: Little was expected of precious metals on Thursday as the market awaited the expiry of options later in the day.
But after that dealers were forecasting weaker prices.

They said the 1330 GMT expiry of so-called over the counter (OTC) options was neutral for gold and silver as most of the option players had bought and sold options at values well away from curent prices.
An option gives its owner the right but not the obligation to buy or sell a commodity at a set price at a set future date.
"It's another excuse for the market not to do anything. But after the expiry is out of the way there is a real risk of gold turning lower," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $382.05 per ounce compared with $382.40 previously and $383.25 on Wednesday morning.
Business was very light early on in Europe, where most metals were trading just below the Wednesday closing level having taken little direction from New York or Asia.
However dealers said orders either side of the current near-static price were building up which could limit movement when the market began to change.
"We have had buy orders at $381.80 which we could not fill yesterday," one dealer said, while others also cited sell orders at $383.00 which were poised to come in on an upward move.
In the background, market sentiment had not been helped by further rumblings about sales of gold from the International Monetary Fund's reserve to boost help for the poorest countries.
Gold was unmoved by the political stability issues arising from questions over Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health.
If gold's forecast move lower came about, one dealer said, a break through the $387.00 support "could become interesting".
That was unlikely near term, but a test as low as $380.00 after the OTC option expiry was a possibility, he added.
Silver was barely traded at $4.90, two cents under the previous close.

Some dealers thought silver was potentially vulnerable to further selling after speculators, disappointed at the market's failure to rise recently, had unload their holdings taking the silver price under $5.00 last week.
"Silver is an industrial metal and the Dow (Dow Jones Industrial Average) is strong yet it seems to have aligned with the oversupplied platinum group metals," one dealer said.
Platinum was indicated $0.75 weaker at $387.25 and palladium was unchanged at $119.25.
Dealers said neither of them was attracting much interest and consumers were happy to run down stocks rather than buy new supplies in an apparently falling market.
